Coupling edges between entities (deprecated)

Source: R/deprecated.R
coupling_entity.Rd

coupling_entity() was renamed entity_network(), because it is not a measure of coupling of its own but the aggregation of the coupling (or co-citation) measures at the level of entities. It is kept as a wrapper, that accepts the former names of the methods ("coupling_strength", "coupling_angle", "coupling_similarity"), and will be removed in a future version.

Usage

coupling_entity(
  dt,
  source,
  ref,
  entity,
  weight_threshold = 1,
  output_in_character = FALSE,
  method = c("coupling_strength", "coupling_angle", "coupling_similarity")
)

Arguments

dt

A data frame or a data.table of direct citations, one row per link between a citing document and a cited reference. It is not modified.

source

Character scalar. The column of the citing documents. Needed to count the documents, not to define the nodes (except for network = "cocitation", see the details).

ref

Character scalar. The column of the cited references.

entity

Character scalar. The column of the entities that are the nodes of the network (authors, journals, institutions...). With network = "coupling" it describes the citing documents (source); with network = "cocitation" it describes the cited references (ref). A document can appear with several entities (one row per entity and reference).

weight_threshold

Number. The minimum number of shared references for two entities to be linked (1 by default). With large entities such as journals, a higher value is advisable.

output_in_character

Logical. If TRUE, from and to are character columns (FALSE by default for this function: they keep the type of the entity column).

method

"coupling_strength" (default), "coupling_angle" or "coupling_similarity": the former names of the methods "strength", "angle" and "similarity" of entity_network(). The Weighting_method column of the result keeps the former name.

Value

See entity_network().
